newsitem.title: UK: Mideast VLCCs fixtures strong, rates steady.
newsitem.headline: Mideast VLCCs fixtures strong, rates steady.

text.p: Continuned strong fixing of large tonnages from Middle Eastern markets helped keep rates healthy on Friday but an adequate supply of ships kept charterers happy, traders said.
At least nine new fixtures were seen for Middle Eastern destinations and a steady trickle of oil also moved westwards.
The market for 250,000 tonne VLCCs saw rates holding their strength at W67.5 for Mideast/Japan routes, while the million-barrel 130,000 tonners were fixed at W84.
Although Idemitsu's fixture of the 240,00 tonne Tokiwa at a hefty W75 was seen as a higher number, it was not seen representative of the market as it was part of a swap deal.
West African markets were steady although oil continues to move eastwards, in addition to normal westwards destinations.

Basis' Suezmax fixture from Angola to the U.S. Gulf at W100 was seen roughly on the market, with vessels twice the size commanding around W60/62.5. Despite good fixing, healthy supply of vessels has kept rates low.

Cross-Mediterranean Suezmax markets were slipping with plenty of ships available. Offers were seen for Sidi Kreir/Sicily routes as low as W95, while 80,000 tonne Aframaxes were being fixed at between W100 and W105.
"There are quite a few offers for the Suezmaxes," one broker said, and quite a few people are looking for Aframaxes."
Few ships of this size are seen left available for November, and the closure of Novorossiisk's Suezmax terminal for maintenance should help boost rates for the Aframaxes.
Inter/U.K.Cont rates for 80,000 tonners were hovering around W100, as are the price of Suezmaxes.
